audit.title: Developer Responsibilities: Market Integrity and Application Code Risks
audit.summary: This is a conceptual risk-disclosure page defining what developers — not Chainlink node operators — are responsible for when integrating Data Feeds. Its biggest strength is crisp, liftable term definitions ("Market Integrity Risks are those associated with external market conditions…") in a clean, well-chunked structure. Its biggest opportunity is discoverability: the page carries **zero structured metadata** (no JSON-LD, missing canonical, no dates) and no symptom/question-phrased headings, so it will lose retrieval to concept-titled queries even though it holds the answer. Honest verdict: solid prose that reads well but is under-instrumented for machine ingestion and under-matched to how developers actually ask liability questions.

recommendations.title: Add structured metadata (JSON-LD `TechArticle` + canonical + dates)
recommendations.issue: measured — "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)… canonical: MISSING… dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential `canonical` URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured freshness/authority signals raise agent trust and parse reliability; absent canonical risks duplicate-attribution loss.

recommendations.title: Add question- and liability-phrased headings/FAQ
recommendations.where: new section near top, plus reworded H3s
recommendations.issue: all headings concept-titled ("Market Integrity Risks"); no query-shaped entry point
recommendations.change: add a short FAQ with headings such as "Who is responsible if a Chainlink price feed is manipulated?", "Is Chainlink liable for oracle price errors?", "What must developers check before integrating a Data Feed?" — answer-first in one sentence each.
recommendations.why: developers query liability by natural question; concept-titled prose loses this retrieval even though the answer ("Developers are solely responsible…") is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add a Market Integrity vs Application Code risk comparison table
recommendations.issue: two risk classes described only in parallel prose; no extractable side-by-side
recommendations.change: table with columns Risk type · Definition · Example factors · Developer mitigation, one row each; put the canonical mitigation links in-cell.
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract *reasons* and build justified answers; improves lift for "types of Data Feed risk" queries.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to risk factors
recommendations.issue: "assets with high market risk, such as those with low liquidity" — qualitative only, vague quantifier "most"
recommendations.change: cite the defined Data Feed risk categories (Low/Medium/High Market Risk labels) inline and name the concrete checks recommended (data-quality checks, circuit breakers, staleness/heartbeat thresholds) as bulleted specifics.
recommendations.why: quantitative/named specifics are among the highest-lift changes; qualitative prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add primary-source / canonical citations
recommendations.change: link definitions of manipulation types and audit expectations to authoritative references (e.g., a glossary or standards page) rather than only the education-hub explainer.
recommendations.why: primary-source inlinks raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Tighten the answer-first opening
recommendations.issue: opens with feed-marketing framing before the responsibility claim
recommendations.change: lead with the liftable one-liner: "Developers — not Chainlink node operators — are solely responsible for monitoring and mitigating market integrity and application code risks when integrating Chainlink Data Feeds."
recommendations.why: a self-contained first sentence resists parametric-prior substitution and is the sentence engines quote.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier "most" (measured) with no threshold; otherwise no keyword stuffing or fluff.
No unresolved cross-references; "(Image: Image)" placeholder at end is a rendering artifact worth removing but not a content defect.
No stale-date signal — but this is because **no date exists at all** (a metadata gap, not staleness).
offPageNotes: Page references `/llms.txt`; confirm this page is listed there so agents can discover it as the canonical responsibilities source.
Site-level: canonical URL and JSON-LD are typically template-controlled — fix at the docs framework layer so all conceptual pages inherit `TechArticle` schema and `dateModified`.
CLI should pass raw `<head>` on the next run; head metadata could not be verified here, so schema/canonical absence is inferred from served HTML only.
